contentBlocks.text: SASSA Grants Without a Bank Account: Cash Collection Guide

Not having a bank account does not disqualify you from receiving SASSA grants. SASSA offers multiple cash collection methods including retail payouts, mobile pay points, and the SASSA card for unbanked beneficiaries. In fact, millions of South Africans receive their grants in cash every month without any bank account.

Not having a bank account should not prevent anyone from accessing social assistance. SASSA provides cash collection methods precisely to ensure unbanked beneficiaries can still receive their grants. The Cash Send system allows you to collect your grant at any major retailer using only your ID and an SMS voucher.

Precious is a 25-year-old from rural Eastern Cape. She does not have a bank account and relies on cash for all her transactions. She applied for the SRD R370 grant and selected 'Cash Send' as her payment method. When her grant is approved, she receives an SMS with a unique voucher code. She takes her ID and the SMS to her nearest Shoprite, where the cashier verifies her identity and hands her the cash. This guide explains exactly how unbanked beneficiaries like Precious can access their grants.

steps.title: Apply for your grant
steps.description: Apply for your grant online via the SRD portal (srd.sassa.gov.za) or at a SASSA local office. Apply for the SRD online or visit an office for other grants.

steps.title: Select 'Cash Send' as payment method
steps.description: During the application, choose 'Cash Send' or 'Retail Collection' as your payment method instead of 'Bank Transfer'.

steps.title: Wait for approval and SMS
steps.description: Once your grant is approved for the month, SASSA will send an SMS to your phone with a unique collection code or voucher.

steps.title: Visit a participating retailer
steps.description: Take your ID and phone with the SMS to any participating retailer: Pick n Pay, Shoprite, Checkers, Boxer, Usave, or Spar.

steps.title: Collect your cash
steps.description: Present your ID and SMS at the till point or collection counter. The retailer will verify your identity and hand you the cash.

contentBlocks.title: Important
contentBlocks.text: Your SMS voucher expires within 7-10 days. If you do not collect your cash within this period, the voucher expires and you must contact SASSA to request a new one. Grants remain available in the system — they do not expire — but the collection window does.

items: Losing the SMS voucher — keep your SMS safe until you collect. If lost, contact SASSA to request a resend
Waiting too long to collect — the 7-10 day window can pass quickly. Collect as soon as you receive the SMS
Sending someone else to collect on your behalf — retailers verify your ID before releasing funds. Only you can collect
Switching to bank transfer then regretting it — you can switch back to Cash Send in the next month's application
Not having a registered SIM card — the SMS voucher is sent to your registered number. Ensure the SIM is in your name

faqs.question: How do I change from bank transfer to cash collection?
faqs.answer: Log into the SRD portal (srd.sassa.gov.za), go to 'Payment Method', and switch from 'Bank Transfer' to 'Cash Send'. Changes take effect from the next month's payment cycle.

faqs.question: Can someone else collect my grant using my SMS voucher?
faqs.answer: No. The retailer will verify your ID before releasing funds. Only the registered beneficiary can collect in person. In exceptional circumstances, a formal power of attorney may be arranged through a SASSA office.

faqs.question: What if I lose my phone with the SMS?
faqs.answer: Contact SASSA toll-free at 0800 60 10 11 to request a resend of the SMS voucher. You may need to visit a SASSA office with your ID to get a replacement.

faqs.question: Can I collect at any retailer, or only specific ones?
faqs.answer: Only participating retailers: Pick n Pay, Shoprite, Checkers, Boxer, Usave, and Spar. Not all retail stores accept SASSA cash collections.

faqs.question: What if I live far from a participating retailer?
faqs.answer: SASSA also offers mobile pay points that visit rural areas on specific dates. Check with your local SASSA office for the schedule in your area.

faqs.question: Can I switch back and forth between cash and bank transfer?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can change your payment method month to month. Changes made before the 20th of the month typically apply to the next month's payment.

faqs.question: Do I need a smartphone to use Cash Send?
faqs.answer: No. Any phone capable of receiving SMS messages works. You do not need internet access or a smartphone.
